statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Evidence Act s.113-B
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 and sentenced to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the mother-in-law of the victim, is alleged to have poured kerosene oil on the victim and set her on fire. The victim sustained severe burns and was taken to the hospital by a neighbor. In the hospital, the victim made a dying declaration stating that she had been subjected to cruelty for dowry and that her mother-in-law had sprinkled kerosene oil on her and burnt her. The victim was married at the age of 22 and had recently become pregnant. The trial court applied the provisions of Section 113-B of the Evidence Act, which presumes that dowry demands were involved in such cases. The victim died within two months of her marriage. The accused was present at the scene of the incident, and the victim also mentioned that her sister-in-law was present but did not make any allegations against the accused.
